title.value: Deep Neural Networks Pruning via the Structured Perspective Regularization
title.justification: The title 'Deep Neural Networks Pruning via the Structured Perspective Regularization' aligns directly with the core methodology presented in the paper.
title.quote: Deep Neural Networks Pruning via the Structured Perspective Regularization

extractions.description: The paper presents a novel method for pruning deep neural networks using a structured regularization term derived from operational research techniques. By applying the Perspective Reformulation technique, the paper introduces the Structured Perspective Regularization (SPR) for structured pruning during training, aiming to maintain model performance while reducing computational complexity. The method is tested on ResNet architectures with datasets like CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, showing competitive results in parameter reduction and accuracy retention.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on machine learning techniques for neural network pruning, without any direct reference to climate change or sustainable development.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In Machine Learning, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are a very powerful tool, broadly used in many applications. Often, the selected (deep) architectures include many layers, and therefore a large amount of parameters, which makes training, storage and inference expensive.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address climate change directly; it focuses on computational methods for pruning neural networks to enhance efficiency.
primary_category.quote: The striking practical success of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) has been initially driven by the ability of adding more and more parameters to the models, which has led to vastly increased accuracy. This brute-force approach, however, has numerous drawbacks: besides the ever-present risk of overfitting, massive models are costly to store and run.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not cover other climate-related topics or mention secondary climate themes.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus is on machine learning efficiency rather than any climate change subcategories, as it mostly deals with reducing computational costs.
primary_sub_category.quote: This works, we develop a novel method to perform structured pruning during training through the introduction of a Structured Perspective Regularization (SPR) term.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no additional climate-related subcategories discussed within this work.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: It is also flexible as it can be adapted to any kind of structured pruning, provided that the prunable entities are known before the training starts.

applications.justification: The focus of the paper is on the efficient pruning of neural networks using the Structured Perspective Regularization method.
applications.quote: We propose a new pruning method based on Operational Research tools. We start from a natural Mixed-Integer-Programming model for the problem, and we use the Perspective Reformulation technique to strengthen its continuous relaxation.
